summary.headline: Jash Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 195 Cr, but INR 46 Cr of Sept-end deliveries stuck in transit cut recognised revenue; FY guidance of INR 875 Cr retained.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 195 Cr (+22% YoY), EBITDA INR 27.3 Cr (+23%) and PAT INR 14.3 Cr (+30%). H1 FY27 revenue was INR 351 Cr (+20%), EBITDA INR 42 Cr (+75%) and PAT grew 239%. Management said around INR 46 Cr of invoiced orders were not recognised because destination-based delivery terms left material in transit at September-end. Consolidated order book stands at INR 955 Cr, of which about INR 625 Cr is overseas, and the company kept its INR 875 Cr full-year revenue guidance, conditional on transit issues easing.

financial_highlights.value: INR 955 Cr (INR 625 Cr overseas, ~INR 330 Cr India)

segments.name: Jash Engineering Ltd (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 227 Cr vs INR 208 Cr last year (+9%), PAT up 18%; order book INR 561 Cr. FY27 revenue target INR 530 Cr. Management said about INR 56 Cr of revenue was recorded in October.

segments.name: Rodney Hunt (US)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 17% and PAT was slightly negative; order book INR 391 Cr (about USD 40 Mn). FY27 target INR 330 Cr; management targets USD 35-36 Mn turnover against USD 25 Mn cited for the prior comparison.

segments.name: Waterfront (UK)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 8% to INR 23 Cr with positive PAT; order book INR 31 Cr. FY27 target INR 60 Cr. A GBP 2.5 Mn order was expected within the month.

segments.name: Jash Process Equipment (ex-WesTech India)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 21 Cr vs INR 25 Cr last year, with negative PAT; order book INR 32 Cr. FY27 target INR 40 Cr. Management said order inflows improved this quarter.

segments.name: Mahr
segments.commentary: Order book INR 27 Cr; FY27 revenue target INR 15 Cr. No Q2 revenue figure was given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of INR 875 Cr retained (JEL 530, Rodney Hunt 330, Mahr 15, Waterfront 60, JPE 40 Cr), conditional on transit-related delivery improvements.
Orders of about INR 46 Cr expected in November and about INR 129 Cr expected to finalise in Q3.
Management expects a strong H2 and sees the order book reaching INR 1,000-1,200 Cr, crossing INR 1,150 Cr in the near term.
Long-term EBITDA margin target of 21-23%; management said margin above 20% is achievable in one to two years as overseas businesses scale.
Capacity from existing India, US and UK plants estimated at about INR 1,200 Cr at optimum load.
capex_capacity: US: new plant contractor expected to be allotted in November 2026; construction to start December 2026 or as per contractor plan; about 12 months to commission. Management gave conflicting timing (end-March 2028 commissioning and December 2027 completion); plant contributes little in FY28, fully from FY29.
Orange (US) facility to be expanded with minor investments to support requirements for about 1.5 years.
Saudi Arabia plant (Dammam, 100% owned) parked for now due to Gulf geopolitical situation; to be revisited next month. Initial plan is assembly and testing before full manufacturing.
Jash Process Equipment: some products now manufactured in Indore instead of fully outsourced.
Data-centre vessels: first order for 4 vessels won in Q2; a further 9-vessel order received; target 20-25 vessels per year, subject to capacity.
demand_pricing: Monthly order intake over the past six months was slightly above INR 60-70 Cr; management said INR 90 Cr per month would equal about INR 1,000 Cr per year.
US/India mix of order book moved from about 75:25 or 70:30 to about 50:50.
Gross margin in H1 was not stated numerically; management said the historical range is 55-60% and FY26 was about 57%.
Tariff refund: USD 0.54 Mn received and booked in consumption cost (not revenue); USD 0.7 Mn pending, of which about USD 0.2 Mn expected this year.
Transit delays on exports (destination-based terms) were the main headwind to revenue recognition.

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence that EBITDA and PAT margins will rise to 13-14% over the medium term given onshoring and US capacity costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the normal EBITDA margin is about 18%, with a 21-23% target as US and UK businesses scale; fixed costs should grow slower than revenue, giving operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin rise in H1 when peers saw compression?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said half-year gross margin moves with order mix and is best judged annually; FY26 was about 57%, within the 55-60% range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to INR 1,000 Cr+ annual order intake?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the order book to exceed INR 1,000 Cr over time, citing new geographies (Vietnam, Indonesia) and products; monthly intake is lumpy and averages INR 60-70 Cr recently.

qa_highlights.question: Why did India growth look subdued and Rodney Hunt diverge?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 46 Cr of invoiced orders at September-end were in transit and not recognised under destination-based terms; the standalone business booked about INR 56 Cr in October.

qa_highlights.question: Is the US plant timeline slipping, and is there capacity headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said existing facilities can deliver about INR 1,200 Cr at optimum load and the US plant will be commissioned around FY28 end; the plant adds little to FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Can employee cost and EBITDA of 20%+ be achieved, and will other income fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said employee cost is normally about 18% of revenue on a full-year basis and that overall EBITDA should move above 20% in one to two years as overseas margins converge.

qa_highlights.question: Update on data-centre vessel orders and acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Data-centre work is taken only when capacity is spare; the first 4-vessel order is in and a 9-vessel order is also received. Acquisitions are being discussed but are premature; an update is expected in about three months.

risks_watch: Export transit delays could keep revenue recognition behind; about INR 46 Cr spillover into Q3.
Achieving INR 875 Cr FY27 revenue requires a steep H2 (H1 was INR 351 Cr), while monthly order intake runs about INR 60-70 Cr versus INR 90 Cr needed.
Jash Process Equipment revenue is down and PAT is negative; turnaround depends on major orders in H2.
Rodney Hunt PAT is slightly negative; US tariff-related uncertainty and the timing of the US plant (contract award, construction, commissioning).
Employee cost and the likely fall in forex and other income could pressure margins, as could the Saudi plan being parked.
summary.management_tone: Confident on full-year guidance and order-book growth, but cautious on near-term delivery timing; Saudi expansion and acquisitions were deferred or left open. Answers on order-run-rate and margin were somewhat hedged, with several figures given inconsistently (for example, the US plant timeline).
key_quotes: As of today, we remain confident of achieving our INR 875 crore revenue guidance.
Most of our orders are on destination -based terms, which means the material has to reach the customer's location before the title gets transferred and we can recognize the revenue.
Once EBITDA comes down from the normal level, bringing it back to those levels takes some time and remains a challenge.
Data centres, this is a new I would say sector for us to address.

adds.what: New US plant (Rodney Hunt), contractor allotment Nov 2026, construction from Dec 2026, ~12 months to commission; timing conflicting (end-March 2028 vs Dec 2027)
Saudi Arabia plant (Dammam) parked due to Gulf geopolitical situation
Orange (US) facility minor expansion to support requirements for ~1.5 years
Jash Process Equipment: some products moved in-house to Indore from outsourcing

growth.why: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of INR 875 Cr retained (+ implied growth not stated as %), backed by INR 955 Cr order book (INR 625 Cr overseas) and ~INR 129 Cr expected to finalise in Q3, but INR 46 Cr of Sept-end deliveries stuck in transit and conditional on easing; US plant only ~12 months from build start, so little FY28 contribution.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management targets 21-23% EBITDA margin over time and says above 20% is achievable in one to two years as overseas businesses scale; H1 EBITDA rose 75% YoY to INR 42 Cr, with operating leverage as fixed costs grow slower than revenue, though Q2 EBITDA margin is about 14% (27.3/195) and the gross margin was not stated numerically.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: FY28 end (US plant); Q4 FY27 construction start
rows.why: US plant contractor award is expected in Nov 2026 with construction from Dec 2026 and about 12 months to commission, but timing conflicts (end-March 2028 vs Dec 2027) and it adds little to FY28; existing India, US and UK plants can deliver about INR 1,200 Cr at optimum load against FY27 guidance of INR 875 Cr.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance of INR 875 Cr is held, but H1 revenue was only INR 351 Cr, so H2 needs about INR 524 Cr (+49% vs H1), and monthly order intake of INR 60-70 Cr runs below the INR 90 Cr needed for INR 1,000 Cr a year; about INR 46 Cr of transit-held revenue spills into Q3.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed, so the case rests on the US plant award in Nov 2026 and Orange expansion for about 1.5 years of need, while the Saudi plant is parked for Gulf geopolitical reasons; the 1,200 Cr capacity against 875 Cr guidance shows headroom for now.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 INR 875 Cr guidance was only retained, and it is conditional on transit delays easing; it would need INR 524 Cr in H2 against INR 351 Cr in H1, so an upgrade is not in view.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Guidance is conditional on transit issues easing, H2 must deliver about 49% more than H1, order intake of INR 60-70 Cr a month is below the INR 90 Cr needed, and JPE revenue fell to INR 21 Cr from INR 25 Cr with negative PAT.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Jash Process Equipment is moving some products in-house to Indore from outsourcing (commissioned), and new geographies (Vietnam, Indonesia) and products are cited for order growth, but no specific launch dates or sizes were given.

rows.label: Order book to INR 1,000-1,200 Cr
rows.when: near term; crossing INR 1,150 Cr soon
rows.why: Consolidated order book is INR 955 Cr, with about INR 46 Cr expected in November and about INR 129 Cr to finalise in Q3, but monthly intake of INR 60-70 Cr is lumpy and needs to reach INR 90 Cr.

rows.label: Data-centre vessel orders (4 + 9 vessels)
rows.why: First 4-vessel order won in Q2 and a further 9-vessel order received, with a target of 20-25 vessels a year, but this is subject to capacity and work is taken only when capacity is spare.

rows.label: JPE turnaround on H2 orders
rows.why: JPE revenue fell to INR 21 Cr from INR 25 Cr with negative PAT, and the FY27 target is INR 40 Cr, so a turnaround depends on major H2 orders against an order book of INR 32 Cr.

tone.note: Management was confident on holding the INR 875 Cr guidance and the INR 1,000-1,200 Cr order-book goal, but cautious on near-term transit delays, and some figures (US plant timing, order run-rate) were inconsistent; analysts probed the H2 revenue ramp, the margin path, and the US plant timeline.
